delivers.runtime: Greedy bounded dispatch (pending bound = workers + queue_depth) into persistent spawn workers via the stdlib-only shim (thread budgets applied before first heavy import); single commit cursor in caller order; staged speculation under .una-batch-staging-<runid>/rowN published by os.replace at commit; coordinator-side digest verification before publish; settings delta applied identity-preserving at commit; composite folded in plan.fold_order; _check_prefix_decisions (observable-prefix invariant) after EVERY commit class including reuse.
delivers.failure_semantics: Plan-error and worker-row failures re-raise the serial exception (exact construction via transportable error args; original type/message preserved for unpicklable exceptions) after the valid prefix committed; batch_report stays None on any raise (serial parity); BatchCancelledError carries the prefix outcomes.
delivers.cancellation: Deadline (budgets work, not spawn readiness), KeyboardInterrupt, worker loss (drain-then-raise: a dead worker's receivable results extend the committed prefix before the cancellation fires); pool reaped, staging removed by the run-level finally (single cleanup owner, ownership-bounded).
delivers.transport: Results travel over a SYNCHRONOUS channel (_ResultChannel over ctx.SimpleQueue: put pickles and writes to the pipe under a POSIX lock, so an abrupt worker death can never truncate an already-completed sibling result — fixed after closure-regression run 1 demonstrated the feeder-buffer loss). Jobs probe-pickled before dispatch (untransportable job fails its own row loudly); worker degrades untransportable results (drop live exception object; then text-only descriptor); _LockSafe carries engine locks across spawn.
delivers.checkpoint_resume: Identity = analysis + semantic profile + backend + package code + spawn shim + python/numpy + input digests + per-row canonical Settings closure + plan summary. Only COMMITTED/SKIPPED units reused; artifacts AND capture payloads digest-verified at resume (failing rows dropped and re-run); reused rows carry output_files/manifest; finalized-composite suppression prevents refold; completed rerun rehydrates final state via one private state-only rerun (timings-budgeted), loud failure when rehydration is impossible.

limitations: Multi-file publication is per-file os.replace at commit (stronger than serial's in-place progressive writes); a hard kill between replaces leaves a partial row visible in the crash window with no journal record — resume re-runs the row and republishes identical bytes. Generation-dir + single-rename protocol deferred (documented).
Hard parent kill leaves .una-batch-staging-<runid> debris; deliberately not age-swept (a concurrent live run's staging must never be removed). Orderly exits always clean by ownership.
output_wStamp=True rows embed per-row worker wall-clock in folder NAMES (time-dependent output on both routes; excluded from bitwise claims).

builtin exception types without transportable args are rebuilt from recorded text (RuntimeError carrying the original type name + message verbatim); transportable args rebuild the exact serial construction.
Rehydration budget scales with journaled row timings (max(120 s, 2x recorded + 60 s)); a slower re-run than 2x its recorded wall aborts typed with the prefix attached and is retryable.

A worker killed mid-result-send (outside the fault-injection phases, e.g. SIGKILL inside SimpleQueue.put's pipe write) can strand a partial message for one recv — inherent to any pipe protocol; the injected faults and OOM kills between jobs are covered by the synchronous channel.
